All 40 results/results/*/sw_results.csv are 181 lines. So 7,200 is Phase 1 alone. verdicts.finding: r13: The tournament is defined as two-phase but 'Phase 3' is referenced five times and never introduced.
verdicts.observed: grep -n 'Phase' paper/main.tex: 2060 ('two-phase tournament'), 2063 (Phase 1), 2065 ('Phase~3 xsim validation'), 2066 (Phase 2), 2073 ('Phase~3 runs xsim'), 2078-2079 ('Phase 1 selects ... Phase~3 measures'), 2782-2783 ('Phase 1/2 ... (Phase 3)'). Four occurrences of the literal token 'Phase 3'/'Phase~3' plus L6's parenthetical, against two defined phases.
verdicts.what_is_true: 'Phase 3' is a leaked internal code name, not a typo. src/sprs_tournament.py:789-790 has the section banner 'PHASE 3: HW SIMULATION WITH TESTBENCH HASHING' and defines run_phase3 (1152) and _load_phase3_done (1129); phase_tag='p1_unified' at 2106. So in the codebase 'Phase 3' names the xsim stage of the legacy three-call organisation (run_phase1 SW -> select_winners -> run_phase3 HW). The campaign used run_phase1_unified, which folds that stage in as 'Step 3' (printed at src/sprs_tournament.py:2148, 2213) of a single pass. The fix is to drop phase numbering entirely, as the draft below does -- cheaper and safer than defining a third phase that then has to be reconciled with a two-phase heading.

Second half REFUTED. I reproduced tables/selbias.tex exactly using the authors' own inclusion rule from paper/scripts/gen_tournament.py:247 ('if len(pairs) < K + 2: continue'): K=10 -> 39 instances, K=15 -> 37, K=30 -> 32, identical from BOTH released HW CSVs (/home/rohit/t05scratch/selbias.py). The per-instance passing counts are 12, 16, 17, 18, 21, ... so requiring >= K+2 = 17 excludes exactly the 12- and 16-configuration instances, giving 37. r05 presumably used >= K+1 or >= K.

What is wrong is one sentence of framing at main.tex:3020-3021 ('The tournament selects candidates for hardware simulation using the compiler's software makespan') and the consumer sentence at main.tex:3041-3043. The numbers themselves are already stated subjunctively at main.tex:3033-3035 ('would have been missed').

verdicts.finding: The 'Feasibility bound' paragraph is counterfactual in three separate ways: the S5 memory pass never ran, the 278 configurations were not rejected, and IMEM was not fixed at 512.
verdicts.observed: (a) S5: enforce_memory is defined at src/sprs_core.py:4942 and called from exactly ONE site, src/sprs_core.py:5676, inside the demo full-pipeline function; `grep -rn enforce_memory src/ experiments/ analysis/` returns no other call. src/sprs_tournament.py contains no reference to enforce_memory, refine_phased or compile_full. The tournament worker (src/sprs_tournament.py:1601-1650) runs S2 -> validate -> S3 -> build_schedule -> generate_instructions and stops. So the S5 stage the paper credits with the 278 rejections did not execute in the campaign. (b) 'Rejected': src/sprs_tournament.py:1637-1647 sets valid=True and only THEN sets error_code=E_IMEM_OF; the testbench is emitted regardless at 1650-1660. Recomputed: of the 278 E_IMEM_OF rows, 117 became dedup leaders and 116 were simulated in RTL, of which 113 PASSED (/home/rohit/t05scratch/, cross-checks T01-X3). (c) IMEM depth: src/sprs_core.py:5380-5384 -- 'max_imem = max(len(progs[g]) ...); imem_sz = 1; while imem_sz < max_imem: imem_sz *= 2; imem_sz = max(imem_sz, 64); dmem_sz = hw.dmem_depth' -- emitted as '.CN_DMEM({dmem_sz}),.CN_IMEM({imem_sz})' at src/sprs_core.py:5432. So every testbench elaborates its OWN IMEM depth, a power of two from 64 upward; the 116 simulated over-budget images have max_imem from 518 to 1792 (median 791), i.e. elaborated IMEM up to 2048. Only DMEM is fixed at 512. The RTL default of 512 (rtl/btree_pkg.sv:19, rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:39) is overridden on every instantiation.
verdicts.what_is_true: The number 278 is correct as a count of E_IMEM_OF rows out of 7,200. Everything the sentence says ABOUT those 278 is wrong: they were not rejected, nothing rejected them, and the 512-entry IMEM they exceed was not the IMEM the fabric was built with. A referee reading src/sprs_core.py:5380 finds this in under a minute, and it currently sits in the methods section three paragraphs above the protocol description that T05 is already rewriting.
verdicts.consequence: REMOVE OR NARROW CLAIM, ~25 words, no new data. This is the highest-risk unlisted item in T05's scope and the cheapest to fix. It also removes an apparent contradiction with T01's finding that IMEM-overflow configurations appear among the RTL-validated set.

verdicts.finding: The dedup leader -- and therefore the (S2,S3) label attached to every simulated configuration and every winner -- is chosen by multiprocessing arrival order, and the paper never says so.
verdicts.observed: src/sprs_tournament.py:2117 iterates 'pool.imap_unordered(_unified_p1_worker, work_items, chunksize=4)'; rows are appended to inst_results[ilabel] in completion order (2124); the dedup loop at 2006-2036 walks that list and the FIRST row carrying a given tb_hash becomes the leader and lends its s2/s3 to the testbench filename ('tb_{s2}_{s3}_none', 2021-2023). The makespan sort at 2045-2048 happens after. This is the mechanism behind T11-D033-ties and T15; I re-derived it here because it is part of 'what actually ran'.
verdicts.what_is_true: The protocol is deterministic in WHICH images are simulated (all of them) and non-deterministic in WHICH ALGORITHM NAME each image is filed under. That asymmetry is exactly why the invariance result is robust and the winner tables are not, and stating it once in Sec. VI-E is the cheapest support T15's rewrite can get.
verdicts.consequence: One clause, shared with T15. Do not duplicate it in both sections.

verdicts.finding: Does 'Phase 3' correspond to anything that ran?
verdicts.verdict: REFUTED (as a campaign stage) / CONFIRMED (as a code identifier)

verdicts.finding: What did the real protocol do that the paper omits and should state?
verdicts.observed: Five omissions, each verified above: (1) coverage of the (S2,S3) grid -- 152 of 180 pairs reached RTL, stated nowhere; (2) the collapse factor -- 6,777 images to 2,920, 56.9%, stated nowhere (logs/phase1_rerun.log:75 'Unique TBs: 2920 / 6777 (56.9% dedup)'); (3) the per-instance simulated range 12-142, median 75 -- only the passing counts 12-141 appear, inside a wall-clock appendix table; (4) the exhaustiveness itself -- no sentence in main.tex says every distinct image was simulated; (5) the maxp_mod_fat disposition -- 5 of 76 attempted, all wall-clock-killed, 71 abandoned, 58.9 core-hours (main.tex:3005 gives the core-hours but not the 5/76).

headline: T05 is confirmed on every checkable point, and what actually ran is better than what the paper claims. The campaign was ONE exhaustive pass, not a two- or three-phase tournament: 40 instances x the complete 18x10 (S2,S3) grid = 7,200 compilations; 6,777 emitted a program image; SHA-256 over the emitted testbench text collapsed those to 2,920 distinct images (56.9%); and every one of them was queued for xsim with no selection of any kind -- 12 to 142 per instance, median 75, covering 152 of the 180 pipeline pairs. The decisive discriminator is not the per-instance counts the reviewers cite but the pair coverage: the shortlist the code CAN build contains 65 distinct (S2,S3) pairs (reproduced exactly from logs/phase1_rerun.log:80-81), and 152 appear in the hardware results, so the described protocol is arithmetically incapable of producing the reported data. 'Phase 3' is a leaked code identifier (src/sprs_tournament.py:789 banner, run_phase3 at 1152) for a function that --mode phase1 never calls; the campaign's own name for that stage is 'Step 3'. Nine of the protocol statements in Sec. VI are false as written and three numbers are wrong or mis-scoped, but only ONE of the fourteen numbers I audited is factually incorrect in value (622, which is a cross-instance count where 641 is the per-instance one, in a table the paper never \input{}s). The rest are right numbers wrapped in wrong descriptions -- which is the cheapest possible failure mode to fix. Two findings are NOT in the docket and matter more than three that are. First, the 'Feasibility bound' paragraph is wrong three ways: the S5 memory pass it credits never executed (enforce_memory has exactly one call site, src/sprs_core.py:5676, in a demo function the tournament never reaches), the 278 configurations were not rejected (117 became dedup leaders, 116 were RTL-simulated, 113 PASSED), and IMEM was not fixed at 512 -- src/sprs_core.py:5380-5383 sizes each testbench's CN_IMEM to the next power of two above its own program length, so the simulated fabrics carry 64 to 2048 entries and only DMEM is fixed. Second, r05's claim that the K=15 row of tab:selbias is off by one is REFUTED: using the authors' own inclusion rule (paper/scripts/gen_tournament.py:247, 'len(pairs) < K+2') I reproduce 39/37/32 exactly from both released CSVs. The appendix's arithmetic needs no repair; only two sentences of framing around it do.
actual_protocol: ONE invocation of run_phase1_unified (src/sprs_tournament.py:1879), split across two runs. SOFTWARE RUN ('--mode phase1 --skip-hw', logs/phase1_sw.log then logs/phase1_rerun.log with --resume): work_items is the full cross product of 40 instances x 18 STAGE2_METHODS x 10 STAGE3_METHODS = 7,200 items (src/sprs_tournament.py:1893, 1959-1975), dispatched over a multiprocessing pool by imap_unordered with chunksize=4 (2117; 72 workers in the first run, 12 in the resumed run). Each item (_unified_p1_worker, 1579-1673) builds the tree and topology, runs S2 assignment, validates it, runs S3 mapping, builds the schedule, emits instructions, records max_imem and imem_ok against a 512-entry model budget WITHOUT acting on it, then emits the full SystemVerilog testbench to a scratch file and records tb_hash = SHA-256 of the entire testbench text (1655). Stages S4 (refinement) and S5 (memory enforcement) are never invoked on this path. When all 180 rows for an instance have arrived, a per-instance dedup fires (2006-2036): rows are walked in ARRIVAL order, the first row bearing each tb_hash becomes the leader, is flagged unique_hw_sim=True, has its scratch file renamed to tb_<s2>_<s3>_none.sv, and is appended to vivado_queue; every later row with the same hash is a follower, its scratch file is deleted, and it inherits the leader's cycle count. The instance CSV is then sorted by makespan and written (2045-2054). Totals reproduced from the released data and matching logs/phase1_rerun.log:74-75 exactly: 6,785 valid, 6,777 with an image, 2,920 unique, 56.9% collapse. select_winners (627-660, a 3-tier makespan threshold capped at 15) then produced 392 rows / 65 pairs into p1_sw_winners.csv, which nothing downstream consumed. HARDWARE RUN ('--mode phase1 --hw-only', no log released): _load_hw_only_state (1795-1877) rebuilds the queue from disk by re-reading every sw_results.csv and enqueueing every row with unique_hw_sim==True whose .sv file exists -- again with no selection. _adaptive_hw_dispatch (1031-1128) runs them through xsim with maxtasksperchild=1, a RAM-based worker cap, an 8 h per-item wall clock, and up to N retries on transient XVLOG/XELAB/timeout codes, which is the origin of the 10 duplicate rows in live_hw_results_p1_maxpe.csv. Outcome: 2,844 distinct images simulated across 39 instances (2,822 passing, 22 non-settling -- see T01); maxp_mod_fat's 76 images were attempted 5 times, all five hitting the wall clock at ~11.8 h each (58.85 core-hours, results/results/live_hw_results_maxp_mod_fat.csv), and the remaining 71 were abandoned. No S4 configuration and no second phase ever entered the pipeline.

corrected_text:
\subsection{Tournament Protocol}\label{sec:method-tour}

Exhaustive cycle simulation of the $22{,}000$-point per-instance space is
infeasible (${\approx}880{,}000$ xsim runs). We fix refinement at the
identity and enumerate the remaining $18\times10$ $(\asgn,\map)$ face
\emph{exhaustively} on every instance: $7{,}200$ compilations, $6{,}777$ of
which emit a program image ($390$ size-gated, $33$ evaluation timeouts).

\emph{Testbench-hash dedup.} Distinct $(\asgn,\map)$ pairs frequently
produce identical program images up to PE relabelling. A SHA-256 hash of the
emitted testbench collapses the $6{,}777$ images to $2{,}920$ distinct ones
($56.9\%$); followers inherit the leader's cycle count. This is not merely a
compute saving: identical images \emph{tautologically} produce identical bit
results, so dedup is what makes each remaining xsim run informative.

\emph{No shortlist.} Every distinct image was simulated --- $12$ to $142$ per
instance, median $75$, covering $152$ of the $180$ pairs --- so no selection
stands between the compiler and the invariance evidence. The $71$ exceptions
belong to \sv{maxp\_mod\_fat}, whose first five runs each exceeded the
$8$\,h simulator budget; it is dropped from the HW-validated suite. A
top-15-by-\sv{makespan} shortlist would have missed a median
\TournLeakPctFifteen{} of the true top-15 by measured cycles
(companion~\S\ref{comp:bias}) --- which is why we did not use one.
